transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Ah, Maestro Salieri! A pleasure to see you, though I confess I did not expect the honour today. Please, come in, come in. How may I be of service? I am the master's journeyman, handling affairs while he is away visiting suppliers.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: 'Lo, Giuseppe. I'm glad I found you here. There's something that needs addressing regarding the new fortepiano we recently purchased for the court. It seems there are some defects in its construction that need to be corrected immediately. I've brought the instrument with me, if you'd like to examine it.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Maestro, it is always a pleasure to hear of the instruments we craft finding their place within the Court's esteemed ensemble. Regarding the fortepiano, you say there are defects? That is most unusual, as our master is meticulous, and every instrument undergoes rigorous testing before it leaves the workshop.

Alas, I cannot personally examine the instrument, as the master builder himself is away. He is travelling to the Black Forest, and then perhaps further east to Bohemia, to secure the finest spruce and maple. He will not be back for several weeks, at least. Would you care to describe these defects in more detail? Perhaps I could note them down for his return.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, I understand the unfortunate circumstances. The defects are quite significant, and I fear they may undermine the quality of the piano's performance. The keys seem to stick, and the pedal mechanism is faulty. Additionally, the tone in the upper register is thin and tinny. I believe this instrument should meet the highest standards of craftsmanship and musicality, and these issues cast doubt on that. I trust you have taken thorough notes, and I eagerly await your master's return so that he can assess the situation himself.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Indeed, Maestro, I am making thorough note of your concerns: sticking keys, faulty pedal mechanism, and a thin, tinny tone in the upper register. These are serious claims, and I assure you I will relay them precisely to the master upon his return.

However, I must also remind you, with all due respect, of the established procedures of our workshop. All commissions from this workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery and acceptance. The Court’s own servants, I recall, signed the receipt confirming the instrument's satisfactory condition at the time of its arrival. Our guild rules, as you may know, are quite strict on such matters, forbidding reopening a completed commission without the master’s personal approval. Therefore, I regret to inform you that I am not authorized to undertake any repair or replacement of the instrument. My apologies, Maestro.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Ah, Giuseppe, I appreciate your understanding of our established procedures. Rest assured, I am not seeking a replacement or repair at this moment. I merely seek assurance that the instrument meets the standards of quality and performance expected from a piano. I trust you will inform the master of my concerns upon his return, and I am hopeful that he will take appropriate action to address these issues. Thank you for your assistance."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Understood, Maestro. I appreciate your gracious understanding. I will, most certainly, relay your concerns regarding the instrument's adherence to our workshop's high standards of quality and performance directly to the master builder upon his return. I will make sure he receives my detailed notes on the sticking keys, faulty pedal, and the tone of the upper register.

As I said, my authority as journeyman does not extend to reopening completed commissions, especially one that has been officially accepted by the Court. That decision rests solely with the master. But you have my word that your message will be delivered promptly the moment he steps back into the workshop.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Giuseppe. Your assistance is greatly appreciated. I am confident that with your expertise and dedication, the master builder will take immediate action to rectify these issues. Until then, I shall keep my fingers crossed, hoping that the instrument will meet the expectations of the court and the musicians. Good day, Giuseppe.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Good day to you too, Maestro Salieri. May your compositions continue to inspire and delight. Do not hesitate to call upon us again for future commissions, should the need arise. We are always at your service.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer

Until then, I remain hopeful that the master builder will rectify the issues with the fortepiano. Farewell, and thank you once again for your understanding.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: You are most welcome, Maestro. I will make sure the master is fully apprised of your hopes regarding the fortepiano immediately upon his return. Farewell for now, and may your journey back to the Court be a pleasant one.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Farewell, Giuseppe. Until we next meet, may you find the same musical inspiration in your creations as I find in the harmonies of your instruments. Safe travels, and thank you once again.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Thank you, Maestro Salieri. Such kind words from a musician of your renown are truly an honour. May the muse guide your hand until our next meeting.
